name: MySQL Migration Assessment
description: Captures MySQL and MariaDB-specific target, compatibility, replication, validation, security and operating decisions that complement automated discovery.

sections.title: MySQL Workload & Target
sections.description: Identify product lineage, database scope, application constraints and the intended target.

questions.text: Which source product is being migrated?
Which databases are in scope, and do applications require cross-database queries?
Is application behavior dependent on case-sensitive table or column naming?
Describe peak periods, batch jobs, reporting cycles and maintenance windows.
Which migration destination and target major version are being evaluated?
options: Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server

sections.title: MySQL Features & Compatibility
sections.description: Decide how discovered engine features, fork differences and application assumptions will be handled.

questions.text: Which discovered MySQL features are business-critical, removable or require replacement?
Are non-InnoDB storage engines required by any application?
Do routines, views, events or triggers depend on specific DEFINER accounts?
Describe dependencies on server plugins, file-system access, custom functions or fork-specific features.
Have source-to-target major-version and MySQL, MariaDB or Percona compatibility differences been assessed?
Does application behavior depend on source character set, collation, sql_mode or time-zone semantics?
Are database proxies, connection routers or load balancers required by applications?
Describe partitioned tables, large LOBs or exceptionally large tables that constrain migration.

sections.title: Migration & Replication
sections.description: Define data movement, replication continuity, connectivity and rollback requirements.

questions.text: What migration method is preferred for this MySQL workload?
Must existing replicas or downstream binlog consumers continue during migration?
Are GTID values required to remain compatible with the existing replication topology?
Have binlog format, retention and downstream-consumer requirements been verified for the migration workflow?
How will auto-increment values be synchronized and protected from collisions at cutover?
Has secure connectivity and sustained migration throughput been tested with production-scale data?
Can database and application changes be frozen during final migration and validation?
Describe the rollback method, data reconciliation process and rollback decision triggers.

sections.title: Validation & Cutover Readiness
sections.description: Define acceptance evidence, performance thresholds, rehearsals and approvals.

questions.text: Which source-to-target validation checks are required for acceptance?
options: Character set, collation and time-zone checks

questions.text: Who owns data reconciliation and can accept documented variances?
Have peak-load baselines and target performance acceptance thresholds been agreed?
options: Baselines captured but thresholds not agreed

questions.text: What is the status of the production-scale migration rehearsal?
Who provides final business, application, database, security and operations sign-off?

sections.title: Security & Operations
sections.description: Capture authentication, encryption, configuration and post-migration ownership requirements.

questions.text: Which authentication methods or plugins must be supported?
Are application connections required to use TLS with certificate validation?
Which global variables or server settings are mandatory, and what is their target disposition?
Who will own backups, version upgrades, parameter changes, monitoring and query tuning after migration?
